title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
statement: Given a list sorted in non-decreasing order (duplicates allowed), return [first index, last index] of the target, or [-1, -1] if it is absent. Aim for O(log n).

hints.1_question: Plain binary search finds some occurrence. What if you ask two different questions instead: 'where does the target first appear?' and 'where do values larger than the target start?'
hints.2_nudge: Write a lower-bound search (first index with value >= x). The first position is lower(target); the last is lower(target + 1) - 1.
hints.3_big_hint: lower(t): lo, hi = 0, len(nums); while lo < hi: mid; if nums[mid] < t: lo = mid+1 else hi = mid. If nums[lower(target)] != target return [-1,-1].

known_bugs.name: returns the single index it happens to find
known_bugs.followup: If the target appears several times, which occurrence does a plain binary search stop at?

known_bugs.name: forgets the - 1 when computing the last index
known_bugs.followup: lower(target + 1) is the first index AFTER the run. Is that the last index of the run?

known_bugs.name: lower bound can't return len(nums)
known_bugs.followup: If the target is the largest value, what should lower(target + 1) return, and what is the biggest value your search can produce?

followups: Why does searching for target + 1 work for integers but not for floats?
How would you count occurrences in O(log n)?
